title: Admissible Arithmetic Liftings and Beilinson–Bloch Height Pairings
subtitle: Shou-Wu Zhang’s construction and the standard conjectures
summary: Zhang’s construction through vertical corrections on arithmetic models, the role of the standard conjectures, and the unconditional case of a product of a curve and a surface.
evidence: Published results are attributed to their precise sources. The general route is conditional on the stated standard conjectures; the curve–surface case is distinguished from that conditional argument.

Zhang’s approach obtains these liftings through the algebraic cohomology of degenerate fibres. Its sufficient input is a standard-conjecture statement on the strata of a semistable model. The proof shows why uniqueness of the lifting is unnecessary. The possible differences of two liftings lie in subspaces that pair trivially with the chosen complementary lift. The height is canonical even when the lift itself is not.

This calculation separates two necessities: a decomposition that allows removal of the vertical part, and detection of the remaining part by the geometric generic cycle class. Establishing a decomposition alone does not prove that a homologically trivial cycle has zero curvature. In the local theory these properties are supplied together by the cited results.

At a finite place of a number field, the generic cycle and its initial closure are defined over the original local field. The vertical correction is represented by cycles on the geometric special fibre. These representatives descend to a finite extension of the residue field. Averaging over a finite Galois extension and dividing by its degree gives a descended rational vertical correction; Galois compatibility of the curvature equation preserves its vanishing. This is the passage to invariant cycle classes used in [2, §2.1].

5. Alterations and normalization of the height

The use of an alteration has two distinct purposes. It can provide a regular semistable model on which the local correction equation is solvable, and it can allow the height of a class on XXX to be computed upstairs. The second purpose requires compatibility of the pairing with pushforward and pullback.

Hypothesis 5.1 (Projection formula on the models used). For each proper generically finite morphism of regular arithmetic models used in the construction, suppose that pullback, pushforward and intersection are defined in the applicable arithmetic intersection theory, preserve zero archimedean curvature where required, satisfy the projection formula, and have f∗f∗=Df_*f^*=Df∗​f∗=D on the relevant classes, where DDD is the generic degree as a morphism over FFF. Suppose also that a vertical class pushes forward to a vertical class, and that pullback preserves numerical admissibility by this projection formula.

These are the precise functorial operations needed in the next calculation. They may be supplied by the classical model height theory on its domain. For a proposed new class of models they must be checked there, especially when a morphism is not flat.

Proposition 5.3 (Independence of a dominating alteration). Suppose a nonempty collection of proper generically finite maps f:Y→XF′f:Y\to X_{F'}f:Y→XF′​, with F′/FF'/FF′/F finite, has the following properties. This proposition isolates the comparison needed when a regular model is reached by alteration. Producing an upstairs intersection number supplies a candidate; the projection formula and a common dominating alteration establish that it depends only on the original cycle classes.

6. The product of a curve and a surface

Theorem 6.1 (Zhang). Let C/FC/FC/F be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve and S/FS/FS/F a smooth projective geometrically connected surface, with FFF a number field. For X=C×FSX=C\times_F SX=C×F​S, the classical construction gives a Beilinson–Bloch height pairing CH⁡2(X)Q,hom×CH⁡2(X)Q,hom⟶R.\operatorname{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbf Q,\mathrm{hom}}\times\operatorname{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbf Q,\mathrm{hom}}\longrightarrow\mathbf R.CH2(X)Q,hom​×CH2(X)Q,hom​⟶R.

The source is [3, §5, Theorem 5.1 and the alteration argument following Remark 5.2]. In the semistable case, the special-fibre components are controlled by the product geometry and suitable blow-ups; the required standard conjectures hold. The general case is obtained by finite extension, alterations of the two factors, and the normalized projection formula. These results provide a worked instance of the route, with the geometric input established rather than assumed.

For the general existence problem, this example suggests a concrete method: identify a class of smooth varieties that can occur as strata of a useful model, prove the required intersection-theoretic assertions for that class, and verify stability under the blow-ups used in the model construction. The difficulty lies in the algebraic cohomology of the resulting strata. Dimension and smoothness alone do not supply the inverse Lefschetz maps in (4.1).

7. A research programme for general varieties

The final target remains (1.1) for all smooth projective X/FX/FX/F and all complementary codimensions. The local and global tasks below have different outputs and can be pursued separately.

Problem 7.1 (Numerically admissible liftings). For each relevant regular projective model Y/R\mathcal Y/RY/R and each α∈Vr(Y)\alpha\in V^r(Y)α∈Vr(Y), prove κYr(α)=0,\kappa^r_{\mathcal Y}(\alpha)=0,κYr​(α)=0, with κYr\kappa^r_{\mathcal Y}κYr​ defined by (3.3); impose the same requirement in the complementary codimension s=n+1−rs=n+1-rs=n+1−r. If the construction is performed after alteration or finite extension, establish the descent hypotheses of Proposition 5.3 for the chosen class of alterations.

This is the direct lifting problem. A solution in both degrees supplies the algebraic input of Theorem 1.1. The zero-curvature complex Green currents then exist by the classical ∂∂ˉ\partial\bar\partial∂∂ˉ-lemma. No choice of a preferred lifting is needed for the resulting pairing.

Problem 7.2 (Standard conjectures on the required strata). Construct semistable alterations for the varieties under consideration and establish (4.1) and (4.2) for every geometric stratum needed in Theorem 4.1. Track the polarizations and prove that the assertions remain valid under the modifications used to obtain the model.

This is a sufficient approach to Problem 7.1. The residual difficulty is an algebraicity and intersection problem on the strata. One may instead try to solve (3.2) directly for the curvatures arising from homologically trivial generic cycles. By Proposition 3.1, that restricted vanishing suffices even if one has not established a full decomposition for every algebraic cohomology class.

Problem 7.3 (An explicit description of the correction). Find finite-dimensional quotients through which the full intersection functional ℓa\ell_aℓa​ and correction map MrM_rMr​ factor, and determine their kernels and images. Prove that the generic homological-triviality condition annihilates the right kernel in Lemma 3.2. Give the correction in a form compatible with pullback, proper pushforward and change of the model whenever those operations are used.

This formulation distinguishes computing the relevant linear system from assuming its solvability. The right-kernel condition is the part that must follow from geometry. A presentation of the matrix without that vanishing leaves the existence problem unchanged.

For the following comparison, let Bp,q\mathcal B^{p,q}Bp,q be the ordinary sheaf of actual δ\deltaδ-forms used in the direct Green-form programme [4, §1]. The word actual specifies a section on the ordinary Berkovich topology, with equality tested against all forms in the indicated sheaf.

Problem 7.4 (Comparison with actual Green forms). Fix the original valued field K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​, a smooth projective X/KX/KX/K, and a prescribed homologically trivial cycle ZZZ of codimension rrr. Starting from a numerically admissible model lifting, construct a form γZ∈Br−1,r−1(Xan∖∣Z∣an)\gamma_Z\in\mathcal B^{r-1,r-1} \bigl(X^{\mathrm{an}}\setminus|Z|^{\mathrm{an}}\bigr)γZ​∈Br−1,r−1(Xan∖∣Z∣an) such that the following integrals exist and satisfy ∫Xan∖∣Z∣anγZ∧d′d′′η=−∫Zanη(η∈Bcn−r,n−r(Xan)).\int_{X^{\mathrm{an}}\setminus|Z|^{\mathrm{an}}}\gamma_Z\wedge d'd''\eta =-\int_{Z^{\mathrm{an}}}\eta \qquad \bigl(\eta\in\mathcal B_c^{n-r,n-r}(X^{\mathrm{an}})\bigr).∫Xan∖∣Z∣an​γZ​∧d′d′′η=−∫Zan​η(η∈Bcn−r,n−r​(Xan)). Prove the identity over the original absolute value and show that the resulting local intersection agrees with the model local height, with the same normalization.

This comparison is an additional analytic problem. The lifting criterion establishes a number by arithmetic intersection; it does not supply a representative in B\mathcal BB or its identity on all actual tests. Conversely, a form construction must still satisfy the arithmetic transformation and reciprocity laws before its global sum can be compared with (1.3).

Finally, Zhang’s LLL-lifting of general Chow classes is a stronger, polarization-dependent construction. His splitting theorem [2, Theorem 2.2.1] uses additional arithmetic standard-conjecture hypotheses. The existence programme here concerns the homologically trivial factors in (1.1). Once their pairing exists, arithmetic Lefschetz, positivity and finiteness can be formulated as further problems for that pairing.

abstractHtml: A homologically trivial cycle can be assigned a height by lifting it to an arithmetic model and making the lift orthogonal to vertical cycles. We give a precise lifting criterion for the resulting pairing, prove independence of the lifts, and express the local correction problem as a linear equation on the special fibre. This identifies the point at which Zhang’s results on standard conjectures and admissible cycles enter the construction. We also give the degree calculation required for descent from an alteration, distinguish this construction from the stronger problem of producing actual non-Archimedean Green forms, and formulate the remaining problems for general varieties. The product of a curve and a surface is a known case of this route.
